chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Sa'd ibn Isma'il from his father Isma'il ibn Isa who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who prays the first (Fajr) prayer, then prays voluntary prayers, and the time of Asr prayer overtakes him before he finishes his voluntary prayer, causing him to delay (in finishing) the Asr prayer. Then he completes his voluntary prayer after Asr, or delays it until he prays it in another time. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He prays Asr and completes his voluntary prayer on another day.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for voluntary prayers interrupted by the time of an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that when the time for the obligatory Asr prayer enters while one is engaged in voluntary prayers, the priority is to perform Asr on time and defer the completion of the voluntary prayer to another day, rather than rushing to finish it or delaying Asr. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of preserving the sanctity of the obligatory prayer's specific time window, even if it means postponing the completion of the nafl. The narration underscores the distinction between the fixed timing of fard prayers and the flexibility of nafl prayers, ensuring that the worshipper does not compromise the validity or timeliness of the primary obligation.
